facts.text: Creola’s name traces back to Creola Bluff, named in 1840 by General Thomas Woodward after a Native American woman he romanticized as an “Indian princess.”.
The Jena Choctaw Pines Casino opened February 13, 2013, on 200 acres of which 40 acres were donated by Mike Wahlder.
Before incorporation, the area that is Creola lay on Choctaw and Caddo lands, where pine woods and waterways supported hunting, trade, and migration along the Buffalo Trail.
Creola was incorporated on January 23, 2002, under Louisiana’s Lawrason Act, becoming a small rural municipality with limited local government services.
U.S. Route 167 cuts through Creola, heading south 11 miles to Alexandria and north 37 miles to Winnfield.
Every home in Creola scores high on heat risk, with 100% of residences facing elevated feels‑like temperatures amplified by humidity.
